saints.name: Antiochus of Palestine

summary.text: A seventh-century monastic writer associated with Palestine. The OCA connects him with a scriptural collection and a prayer used at Compline.
summary.reason: A concise source-bound account of the saint's life, identity and death; the linked modern source is not reproduced in full.

saints.context: The Church's published hagiographic account is distinguished from independently established chronology. Unknown dates and circumstances are left unspecified.

blocks.text: Antiochus came from Galatia. The published life places him during Emperor Heraclius’s reign, 610–641.
blocks.reason: A concise source-bound account of the saint's life, identity and death; the linked modern source is not reproduced in full.

blocks.text: The OCA reports that he witnessed the killing of monks at Saint Sabbas’s monastery and recorded their sufferings. This identifies him as their witness and chronicler; the account does not say that he was killed with them.
blocks.reason: A concise source-bound account of the saint's life, identity and death; the linked modern source is not reproduced in full.

blocks.text: This short life supplies neither a death date nor a manner of death. Those details remain unspecified.

blocks.text: His Pandect of the Scriptures treats biblical moral teaching in 130 chapters. The OCA also notes an attribution in the Evergetinos and identifies a prayer associated with sleep in the service of Compline.
